Hi Aisha,

Thanks for taking time today — sharing the notes from our internal ops sync so we have clear constraints ahead of your provisioning work. Key points:

- Primary region must be US-West (their latency targets are 50–75ms p95 for inference).
- We will need a warm pool of 4x A100-equivalent GPUs for our 3-week pilot window, with a burst target up to 12x for weekends.
- Procurement requires proving autoscale backfill for burst events (they run heavy batch jobs overnight).

Attached is our simplified traffic seasonality matrix. Can Redwood confirm whether the warm pool + burst approach maps cleanly to your multipool routing? If not, we need an alternate suggestion before procurement completes.

Elena
Ops Lead — Novalabs

Attachment: novalabs_multipool_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 74KB)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-05 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staging pool routing & burst policy decisions — Novalabs Dedicated

Hi Elena — thanks for the matrix, that helps. Short answers and next steps below.

Answers:
- Yes, we can anchor the primary workload in us-west and route failover to us-east within the same Dedicated estate.
- Warm pool sizing (4x) looks fine for steady-state pilot. For weekend bursts to 12x, we recommend a two-tier burst policy:
  1) Scheduled burst window: pre-warm additional instances using rapid warm-start (20–30m) policy.
  2) On-demand burst: ephemeral capacity from cloud partners (we'll prefer same region where possible) with graceful degradation policy to reduce context-size per request if capacity is constrained.

Open questions (please confirm):
- Are procurement timelines fixed (you mentioned 3 weeks)?
- Do you need cross-AZ redundancy inside us-west or is a single AZ acceptable for the pilot?

Next steps:
- Ben will draft a staging pool routing diagram and a proposed burst-rule PDF for procurement.
- Monica will propose the autoscale cooldowns / metrics (cpu/gpu-util + queue depth) we plan to enforce during pilot.

I'll loop in Sean from Ops to validate the runbook items and final SLA exceptions.

Best,
Aisha
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachment (to follow): proposed-burst-rules-v1.pdf

Elena / team — attaching a short diagram and the burst-rule draft for procurement. High-level logic included in the PDF. Callout items:

- Routing: Pilot traffic will be pinned to Pool-A (us-west primary). Pool-B (us-east) configured as cold standby; warm-start windows can be scheduled nightly.
- Autoscale triggers: GPU utilization > 68% sustained for 3 mins OR request queue depth > 120 -> scale +1 instance. Scale-down: utilization < 40% and queue depth < 20 for 10 minutes.
- Weekend scheduled burst: cron window Fri 22:00 -> Sun 06:00 where we pre-warm to target capacity.

If procurement needs a guaranteed warm-start <30m SLA for added capacity we can include an SLO clause in the activation MSA; that will affect price/commitment.

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-burst-rules-v1.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

- We do need single-AZ for the pilot to reduce networking complexity, but cross-AZ is required for GA later. Marking that in the procurement doc.
- The warm-start <30m SLO is acceptable for procurement as long as there is a clear fallback plan (degradation to smaller context windows).
- Can Redwood provide a runbook snippet that shows the fallback behavior (what is reduced, how we surface degraded metrics to our engineers)? Procurement will attach that to the PO.

If you can drop that runbook snippet before EOD Thursday we can keep to our procurement cadence.

Elena

Elena — quick runbook snippet for procurement (copied below). I also attached a one-page flow you can paste into the PO.

Runbook snippet (procurement-friendly):
- Trigger: When GPU utilization >= 68% for 3 minutes OR queue depth >= 120, Redwood autoscaler will add one GPU instance to the active pool. For scheduled burst windows the system will pre-warm to the configured capacity 30 minutes before window start.
- Fallback: If on-demand capacity is not available within 30 minutes, Redwood will return degraded responses that reduce context-length by 50% and switch to a reduced-token-mode. All degraded requests will include an x-rw-degraded header and a degradation_reason code in the body.
- Observability: Metric feeds pushed to Novalabs via the Redwood Console include per-route p95 latency, token cost, active_instances, queue_depth. Alerts: active_instances==capacity && queue_depth>200 -> alert Novalabs on-call and Redwood SRE.
- Escalation: If degradation persists > 60 minutes, Redwood will trigger manual escalation and open a bridge with Novalabs and our cloud partner.

Please find the one-pager attached: it summarizes the triggers, fallback and observability endpoints. Happy to iterate quickly if procurement needs different wording.

Monica
Implementation Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachment: runbook-onboard-onepager.pdf (PDF, 12KB)
